We are an early-stage, venture-backed AI infrastructure company building production-ready Kubernetes-based systems for GPU-intensive workloads. Our platform helps companies go from bare metal to fully operational AI clusters in days, and we're looking for a Java Developer to join our small, high-impact engineering team.

What You'll Do

  • Understand customer requirements and translate them into robust, scalable Java-based solutions.

  • Design, develop, and maintain backend services and infrastructure tooling that supports our distributed systems platform.

  • Collaborate closely with product and infrastructure engineers to deliver features end-to-end.

  • Contribute to the reliability and performance of systems handling AI inference pipelines, distributed training, storage orchestration, and GPU scheduling workloads.

  • Participate in code reviews, architectural discussions, and continuous improvement of engineering practices.

What We're Looking For

  • Required:

    • Solid hands-on experience with Java development and the JVM ecosystem.

    • Familiarity with distributed systems concepts and cloud-native environments.

    • Experience working with or around Kubernetes, containerization (Docker), or related infrastructure tooling.

    • Strong problem-solving skills and ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, early-stage environment.

    • Clear communication skills â we are a small team and direct collaboration matters.

  • Nice to have:

    • Experience with GitOps workflows or tools (e.g., Flux, ArgoCD).

    • Exposure to GPU scheduling, ML infrastructure, or high-performance computing environments.

    • Familiarity with open-source contribution practices.

    • Experience in a startup or early-stage company setting.

Compensation & Benefits

Compensation details were not provided for this role. This is a full-time position at an early-stage, VC-backed company where equity participation is typical. Details will be discussed during the interview process.

Location

This role is based in Los Angeles, CA, USA. The company also has a presence in San Francisco, CA.

Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.

title: Donât Put Yourself a Box
description:
Photo by Piotr MusioÅ / Unsplash

Donât Put Yourself in a Box

Personal Development and Career Growth

  • Apr 26, 2024

Summary

  • Companies need "boxes" (job classifications) to grow and function. This makes hiring, compensation, and career development tractable, and promotes fair treatment of employees.
  • If the boxes are too large, a company can't grow. If the boxes are too small, innovation and ownership are smothered.
  • The size of a company's boxes is directly proportional to the level of trust employees have for management.
  • To get hired, put yourself in the box the company is hiring for. Tailor your resume to highlight those skills and experiences; put yourself out there as a âspecialistâ in the thing theyâre hiring for.
  • If aiming for a promotion, demonstrate how your work embodies the behaviors and impacts of the next-level âboxâ.
  • Don't let those boxes define you. Your value and identity goes far beyond any job description.

Hot Take

Businesses can't function at scale unless they put people in standardized "boxes"; if you want to be hired and to grow your career, you need to understand that, and understand how to work with those boxes. On the other hand, you can't be reduced to a box, and if you tie your identity to those boxes in your thinking, you'll limit yourself in ways that are unnatural and harmful.

This is like the paradox of SchrÃ¶dinger's Cat, both alive and dead at the same time. Like with quantum mechanics and the cat, whether youâre in a box or not depends on whoâs doing the measuring: your employer, or you.

My Box Origin Story

My introduction to the idea of âboxesâ came in the late 2000s, when I noticed that people at Google were having a hard time getting hired or promoted if they were doing âoperationalâ work that didnât involve much traditional program management. Whether they were being considered for hiring or promotion, they were told, essentially, âYouâve done some great work, but itâs not program management; weâre not sure what role/ladder is a fit for you, but itâs not this one. Next!â

This was clearly a problemâeven though they didnât do PERT diagrams and Gantt charts, Googlers did important work in these roles, and roadblocks to hiring and promoting them created both operational and retention issues as jobs went vacant and high-performing employees felt their value wasnât being recognized. As a member of both Program Management hiring and promotion committees at Google I had more visibility to this issue than most others; I spoke to a friend of mine in People Operations (Googleâs HR), who turned out to already be well aware of this problem from repeatedly dealing with upset hiring managers and frustrated promotion candidates. Together, we hatched a plan: to create a new job ladder (job classification) for these âoperationalâ program managers to move to, that was better suited to the type of work they did.

We gathered some data, wrote a proposal, and set up a meeting with the SVP responsible for all engineering at Google. The SVP had been in quite a few meetings Iâd presented to before; I knew him to be not only a brilliant and capable leader, but a genuinely nice guy, too, so I had no worries about the meeting. Imagine my shock then, when this âgenuinely nice guyâ started yelling at us, telling my partner and I that we were going to wreck Google culture!

I vividly remember what he said: âDONâT PUT PEOPLE IN BOXES!â He told us Google needed some job classifications, but that our culture required those classifications to be both broad and vague so both employees and their managers wouldnât be blocked from doing whatever needed to be done. The worst thing we could do, the SVP told us, was to make the classification âboxesâ so small people could say âthatâs not my jobââwhich is precisely what he saw us proposing to do!

A year or two before this Google had shifted from having just three job types (over-broadly, they were âengineersâ, âtechnical people that donât do engineeringâ, and âeveryone elseâ) to having around around a dozen (one of which was my ladder, âTechnical Program Managersâ). There had been a lot of debate about whether those boxes were already too smallâ¦ but the senior team had decided 12â15 job categories were acceptableâenough large boxes to make hiring, career development, and compensation more efficient, but not so many that jobs were defined too narrowly. We left his office dejected, but also enlightened: it said a lot to me that this SVP thought it so important to Googleâs culture, a lesson Iâve never forgotten. (Times have changed though; Google now has many more job ladders, including at least 5â10 âoperationalâ ladders broken off from Program Management well beyond what my friend and I had proposed).

Why Companies Need Boxes

Why do we need âboxesâ (job classifications) at all? Wouldnât the world be better if everyone just did whatever they saw that needed doing? The value of boxes to corporations comes down to two things: scaling and trust.

Scaling

If youâre in a small startup, you want employees who can wear many hats, and who wonât feel limited by things like job titles. Because there are so few employees, and because you know everyone personally and need everyone you hire to have an outsized impact, you can afford to put a lot of energy into every individual hiring decision. Compensation planning is pretty lightweight and customized, both because there arenât many people to deal with, and because you want to compensate people based on their contribution to the business, regardless of what their title is. Everyone is a âspecial snowflakeâ.

That changes quickly as your startup growsâyou cross a line where it becomes infeasible to treat every hire as a unique individual, with bespoke hiring and compensation. This is where âboxesâ become necessary: you have to put people into categories, with standards for how hiring, compensation, and career progression work for each boxâitâs the only way you can scale the company. The alternative to this would be to allow an increasing number of managers to continue bespoke hiring and comp within their own areasâ¦ which leads to the second issue, trust.

Trust

Because startups are so risky, the ability of potential employees to trust the founders is a big dealâif they donât appear trustworthy, theyâre not going to attract the kind of people they need. As the company grows, the number of managers that both employees and senior management need to trust grows, too. At some point it becomes too much: employeesâ willingness to âhave faithâ that managers will make fair and appropriate decisions drops lower and lower, so much so that everything will fall apart without the enforced fairness of standardized boxes.

ð¡

The size of the boxes in a company are directly proportional to the amount of trust employees have in management

Labor unions are the endgame for this sort of trust problem. One of the big rallying points for companies trying to avoid unionization is always to try to convince employees that management has their best interests at heart, and can be trusted. As a rule, unions have close to zero trust for management, andâas a direct consequenceâunions often push for the smallest âboxesâ possible: boxes for very narrow roles, subdivided by seniority, and sometimes further subdivided by location. They see this as the best way to ensure fairness in an environment where management canât be trusted at all. This is the ultimate version of the cultural harm my SVP was worried about.

Boxes and Hiring

Scaling and trust drive companies to put employees into standard categories, or boxes. How do those boxes affect hiring, and, understanding this, how can you better âsellâ yourself as a candidate for jobs?

Most companies above startup size need to hire for boxes, for the reasons given above; itâs just too much work to do anything else. It would be wonderful if recruiters, interviewers, and hiring managers had the time to carefully read and savor every resume that came in, and then spend time meeting with every candidate to pull out nuances that didnât come across clearly in their job histories. Thatâs not the world we live in, though; there are too many candidates to get through, and too few hours in the day.

The usual practice is for recruiters to work with hiring managers to identify standard requirements (boxes, again!) that can be used to screen out people and reduce the number of candidates they need to go into more depth with (hiring managers will usually never see any of those dropped candidates). Those standard requirements are typically based on a template used for all jobs of the same ladder and level, extended with custom specs tailored to the particular role being hired for. In the language Iâve been using in this article, the job requirements are a very clear âboxâ, and the screening process only lets through candidates whose âshapesâ fit that box, like a childâs sorting toy.

Source: Flickr user rosipaw, CC BY-NC-SA 2.0

When there are lots of candidates for a tiny number of jobs, the recruiters donât magically get more time to handle the extra candidatesâinstead, they often deal with the overload by tightening the screening criteria even further: that is, by making the boxes smaller.

Behaviorally, the shift from âstartupâ to âbig companyâ, and the shift from rapid growth to slow growth, show up to candidates as employers become increasingly selective. Startups like generalists; big companies like specialists. If there are few people vying for each job, hiring managers won't care as much about past experience; if there are many candidates, theyâll only be interested in people whoâve previously done the same kind job theyâre hiring for. These trends are amplified when business is tough and hiring budgets are thin: hiring managers become nervous about using their scarce headcount on unproven candidatesâthey need people who have already shown success in exactly the job the manager needs done.

ð¡

Iâm writing this in April, 2024, in a time of high interest rates and widespread layoffs in tech, and when there are lots of AI-based screening tools being offered that promise to save recruiters time; you do the math about the current hiring marketâ¦

Besides being lucky, there are two powerful ways to cut through âsmall box screeningâ:

  • Put yourself in the box theyâre hiring for. This means customizing your resume for each job you apply for, or at least for each type of job youâre going after. If theyâre hiring for someone with experience doing X, focus your resume on how youâve been successful doing X (or at least, things like X) in the past. When a recruiter or hiring manager looks at your resume, you want them to jump out of their chair and exclaim: âwow, this person is exactly what weâve been looking for!â
  • Pull a Kobayashi Maru by bypassing the whole screening process: use your network of personal connections to get an introduction to the hiring manager. This is probably the single most powerful thing you can do because it exposes you to the hiring manager as a whole person, instead of a peg that fits in a box.

Boxes and Promotions

A similar situation arises with promotions: the people making decisions about whether you should be promoted or not donât (usually) have the familiarity with you, or the time, to make a customized decisionâ¦ and doing so would create fairness issues. Instead, they look at whether you fit the next-level box. I want to talk about two parts to this: one related to the job ladder, and one related to the level.

Job Ladder

I vividly remember one promotion committee I served on, where we were deciding whether or not to promote an individual who had unquestionably performed at the next levelâ¦ but the work theyâd done wasnât consistent with the job ladder (work classification) they were assigned to. They had delivered amazing business impact through striking personal initiative, leadership, and hard workâ¦ but what theyâd done had nothing in common with the sort of work expected for the job ladder, or âboxâ, they were in. Should we promote them, or not? We debated the question for far longer than weâd spent on any other candidate weâd reviewed, called in HR support to advise us, andâ¦ we couldnât decide. The rules were that âif you canât decide, the decision needs to be ânoââ, so we ended by turning down the promotion and recommending the person for a large cash bonus, instead. Our decision was appealed, and the appeal was denied, too, for the same reason: despite the great work, the candidateâs work was outside the box.

Sometimes the process and people deciding on your promotions will be more amenable to âoutside the boxâ work, but really, regardless of whoâs making the promotion decision, and what their ârules of engagementâ are, your chances of success will be greatly enhanced by you being aware of the box imposed by your job ladder as you go about your work, and as you explain that work to others. To be clear: Iâm not saying to limit what you work onâthatâs the ânot my jobâ problem the SVP at the beginning of the article was talking about! What I am saying is that you should proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways consistent with the box.

For example, if youâre a Program Manager and spent a lot of time creating product requirements (the work of a Product Manager at most companies), when you and your direct manager describe it to others, be sure you both talk about (for example) the work you did to understand what other work was dependent on having the requirements, how you delegated and tracked some of the work on market research, bringing it all together into a single document, how you built consensus on the requirements, communicated them to the engineering team, and then managed scope creepâall things that are part of the description of the Program Management box. This makes it easy for the people who will decide on your promotion to say âHuzzah! They did both the Program and Product Managementâ, instead of saying âThis was great Product Management, too bad theyâre a Program Manager.â

Job Level

Really, this is a topic that deserves (and will get) an article all on its own, but I think itâs relevant to surface it here: in general, higher level jobs arenât just harder/bigger/broader versions of lower level jobs: theyâre different âboxesâ altogether. The next-level behaviors senior people are looking for are often behaviors that arenât exercised much, if at all, at your current level. I think of these as âphase changesâ, analogous to the phase changes water goes through as it turns from solid ice to liquid to gas as you turn up the heat: itâs always the same water, but it looks and behaves differently in each phase. Some of these transitions are more abrupt and noticeable than others, but theyâre definitely there. At Google for example, there are noticeable differences between all levels, but the âphase changesâ are especially acute between levels 5 and 6, and between levels 7 and 8.

The takeaway here is that you can greatly increases your chances of success by understanding what those âphase changesâ are (more senior mentors can be super helpful in this)âwhatâs qualitatively different about the next-level boxâand then work with your manager to proactively plan how you will describe your work in ways that highlight those qualitative differences.

Boxes and You

So after telling you about the importance of âboxesâ, now Iâm going to tell youâ¦ to avoid them!

This sure looks like a paradox, but let me explain!

Weâve been talking about how companies, managers, and recruiters use boxes, and how, because of scaling and trust, itâs just not practical for them to operate in any other way. Weâd hope that they donât make the boxes too small, and that they have good judgment in how they apply themâ¦ but boxes are a fact of life in the world of work.

The place where you should avoid boxes isnât in the workplace, though: it's in your head. Itâs completely natural for peopleâs occupation and organization to become a part of their identityâ¦ but it's harmful to let that go too far: you are not your job, and you are not your job title.

A lot has been written about the psychology of tying oneâs identity to their job, but the thing I want to focus on here is how putting yourself in a box in your own thinking (e.g. seeing yourself as a âProduct Managerâ, as a âGooglerâ, and so on) can mean putting counterproductive limits on your own behavior, and your own thinking about whatâs possible.

ð¡

Youâre much more than, and much more capable than, the box youâre in.

From a career perspective, itâs a good practice to periodically take some time out and take stock of where you are now and how that fits with where you want to go. If you do this sort of self-assessment youâll often decide youâre basically on the right path and just need to make some minor adjustmentsâ¦ but sometimes youâll realize that the path youâre on wonât take you where you want to be, and that bigger changes are needed: maybe you should ask your manager for different responsibilities? Change teams? Change job ladders? Even change companies? All of those require seeing beyond the box youâre in.

Even though you need to describe yourself in terms of boxes to get where you are now, if your own thinking is constrained by those boxes, it will be hard for you to see that maybe the best path for you is quite different from the one youâre on. Maybe you should change teams? Roles? Departments? Even change your city, or your employer? Donât get me wrong: I know plenty of people whoâve been in more or less the same job, in the same place, working for the same company, for many years, and theyâre very happyâ¦ but itâs also common for people stay in the same role because they see that role defining them, instead of just being something they do.

How You Can Bring Order From Chaos, Today

Here are some things you can do now to apply these ideas:

  • If youâre looking for a job now, describe yourself as being well inside the box your potential employer is hiring for: tune your resume to the job youâre going after. You should have a different resume at least for every âclassâ of job, and sometimes for each specific job. It can be hard to do it if youâre going after several types of job at the same time, but your LinkedIn resume needs to support the more focused, specialized resumes youâre using. Make sure you highlight the skills and expertise called out in the job ads youâre applying to, and talk about your skill and experience in that area. No one hires generalists, so donât call yourself one in your resume; instead, describe yourself as a specialist in the very thing your target company is hiring for.
  • If youâre working toward a promotion now, put yourself in the box you want to be promoted to. Ask your manager and mentors to help you understand the heart of the next-level box, and think about how you can describe your work, behavior, and accomplishments in terms of that box.
  • Donât tie your identity to the box youâre in. You are a complete person with a personality, skills, and experience that transcend any mere box, and if you tie up your identity with the boxes other people put you in, you will limit the paths you can take and the things you can accomplish.

What Do You Think?

I'd love to hear about your experiences with boxes! If you're a paid supporter of this newsletter (hint, hint!) you can add comments below.

title: Why do you want this new job
description:
No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â

In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:

  • Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.
  • Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.
  • Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.
  • Iâm looking for more challenging work.

All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills

Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.

About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.

If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.

About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.

Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.

In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating.

title: Background job monitoring
description:
• Glossary/
  • Scheduled Jobs/
  • Background job monitoring

Scheduled Jobs

Background job monitoring

Background job monitoring is watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals.

What is background job monitoring?

Background job monitoring describes watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. In reliability work, the label is useful only when it maps to a measurable check, a clear owner, and a next action when expectations break. Without that operational meaning, the phrase becomes decoration in dashboards and status updates.

Why it matters

Background job monitoring matters because teams need a precise shared meaning for watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals. Vague language turns incidents into arguments about words instead of fixes.

When everyone uses the same definition, alerts, status updates, and post-incident reviews stay aligned.

How it works

In practice, watching asynchronous jobs for timely completion and success signals shows up as a concrete signal you can measure or communicate. Operators define what good looks like, watch for deviations, and record what happened when expectations break.

The useful version of background job monitoring is operational: it changes who gets notified, what customers see, or which metric a team reviews after an incident.

Practical example

Imagine a team operating around queue worker heartbeat each minute. When observed behavior stops matching the definition of background job monitoring, the team treats that change as a reliability event with a clear owner and next step.

Common misconception

Background job monitoring requires browser scripting

That reading usually collapses distinct ideas into one slogan. Keep background job monitoring tied to observable behavior so the definition stays useful under pressure.

How Fajita handles this

Use heartbeats or success pings from workers. External HTTP monitors alone may not see queue lag.

title: Resource Manager
description:
Company Description

The Story Shack is a modern, low-overhead creative studio built to scale a brand's story. We give brands the power of an in-house creative team â without the headaches and high costs that plague the industry. We address the broken creative model by offering flexible, budget-friendly, scalable, and specialized solutions for brands.


Role Description

We're on the hunt for a sharp and dependable operator to join our scrappy, fast-growing creative studio and work directly alongside our Head of Community.


As our Resource Manager, you'll be the engine behind the scenes â running talent outreach, supporting creative resourcing, coordinating project needs, and keeping administrative tasks tight and on track. You'll help make sure every project has the right people in place at the right time, and that nothing falls through the cracks.


You'll also get exposure to the business side of a growing agency â supporting resourcing, budgeting, invoicing, and talent relationships as we continue to grow.


If you've got real experience in the agency, studio, or production world, love staying organized amid creative chaos, and want a front-row seat to how a creative company is actually run, this role was made for you.


Responsibilities

  • Manage daily tasks with our 300-person creative community, including administrative outreach to freelance talent such as creative directors, copywriters, directors, cinematographers, photographers, producers, designers, and more â including initial outreach, scheduling, and follow-up.
  • Run availability and rate checks across our talent network for upcoming projects, keeping records accurate and up to date.
  • Support creative resourcing with Project Managers, Account Managers, and Producers by helping match the right talent to the right projects based on skill set, client needs, availability, and budget.
  • Handle financial administration, including invoice monitoring, payment tracking, and flagging discrepancies.
  • Maintain organized, up-to-date talent and project databases.
  • Serve as a first point of contact for talent inquiries and applications, while helping build and maintain strong relationships across our creative community.


Qualifications

  • Experience in a creative agency, studio, or production environment with resourcing responsibilities.
  • Outstanding communication and organizational skills.
  • Comfortable managing multiple tasks and projects simultaneously.
  • Detail-oriented, especially when it comes to financials and scheduling.
  • A collaborative, low-ego attitude with the ability to support someone else's workflow and priorities.
  • Genuine interest in the advertising and film industries and building relationships with creative talent.
  • Familiarity with talent databases, project management tools, and invoicing/accounting software is a plus.
  • Existing relationships within the creative production community are a plus.

Senior Product Manager, Technical (m/f/d)
Teamleiter Sales Dortmund
description:
Über Salonkee

Wir bei Salonkee glauben, dass Friseure und Beauty- Expert:innen ihre Zeit mit Handwerk und Kreativität verbringen sollten - nicht mit Zettelwirtschaft. Als eines der am schnellsten wachsenden SaaS-Unternehmen Europas bieten wir Salons eine Komplettlösung: von der smarten Online-Buchung bis hin zu automatisierten Zahlungen.

Wir suchen keine Verwalter, sondern Gestalter. In Dortmund schlagen wir das nächste Kapitel auf und suchen jemanden, der unser lokales Team nicht nur führt, sondern gemeinsam mit uns wächst.

 

Deine Rolle: Mitmacher, Stratege & Mentor

Du bist das Gesicht von Salonkee in Dortmund. Deine Aufgabe ist es, ein schlagkräftiges Team aufzubauen und gleichzeitig sicherzustellen, dass wir nah am Kunden bleiben.

  • Teamaufbau & Coaching: Du baust das Team auf ca. fünf Talente aus. Du führst keine Excel-Tabellen, sondern Menschen - durch 1:1s, gemeinsames Training und echtes Feedback.

  • Präsenz im Markt: Du bist kein Büromensch. Du begleitest dein Team zu Terminen vor Ort, unterstützt bei der Kaltakquise und zeigst in Live-Demos, wie Salonkee den Alltag der Salonbesitzer erleichtert.

  • Struktur schaffen: Du organisierst die Woche so, dass dein Team Erfolg haben kann. Du behältst die CRM-Pflege und die Kennzahlen im Blick, um frühzeitig zu sehen, wo wir nachjustieren können.

  • Vorbildfunktion: Gerade am Anfang bist du selbst aktiv im Verkauf tätig. Nicht, um Rekorde zu brechen, sondern um den Markt in Dortmund im Detail zu verstehen.

 

Das bringst du mit

  • Erfahrung im Außendienst: Du hast 2–4 Jahre Erfahrung im Vertrieb (idealerweise B2B) gesammelt und weißt, wie man Türen öffnet.

  • Lust auf Führung: Du musst noch kein „Director“ gewesen sein, aber du hast das Talent, andere zu motivieren und Verantwortung für gemeinsame Ziele zu übernehmen.

  • Strukturierte Arbeitsweise: Du planst deine Region eigenständig und weißt, wie man Prioritäten setzt.

  • Kommunikation: Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und kannst dich sicher auf Englisch mit unserem internationalen Team austauschen.

  • Mobilität: Für die Termine bei unseren Partnern vor Ort ist ein Führerschein notwendig.

 

Warum Salonkee?

  • Sicherheit & Erfolg: Ein attraktives Gehaltspaket aus Fixum & Provision, das deine Leistung wirklich belohnt.

  • Dein Firmenwagen: Auch zur privaten Nutzung - damit du immer flexibel bleibst.

  • Freiraum: Wir vertrauen dir. Deine Arbeitszeit gestaltest du so, wie es für dich und dein Team am besten passt.

  • Echte Benefits: 50 € monatliches Guthaben (steuerfrei) via Probonio für deine persönlichen Bedürfnisse sowie regelmäßige Teamevents, die diesen Namen auch verdienen.

     

Klingt nach deinem nächsten Schritt? Wir machen es kurz: Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf. Wir freuen uns darauf, dich kennenzulernen und gemeinsam Dortmund zu erobern!

title: Head of Music
description:
About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Today, we serve millions of users and thousands of businesses - from fast-growing startups to large enterprises like Deutsche Telekom and Meta. Our investors are some of the world's most prominent, including Andreessen Horowitz, ICONIQ Growth and Sequoia. We've raised $781M in funding and our last valuation was $11B - multiples of 11, always.

We have expanded from voice into three main platforms:

  • ElevenAgents enables businesses to deliver seamless and intelligent customer experiences, with the integrations, testing, monitoring, and reliability necessary to deploy voice and chat agents at scale.

  • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

The ElevenLabs Music team is entering its next phase of growth. After gaining significant traction across enterprise, creator, and artist products, we're expanding our leadership team to accelerate product development, licensing, partnerships, and go-to-market across our music business.

We are hiring a Head of Music to lead our enterprise and consumer music business end to end. We have the best AI music and audio researchers and world-class music models - built in partnership with artists, labels, and publishers. We’re doubling down on music and seeking an experienced industry leader to guide us into the future. We intend to be the defining AI music company. Our Head of Music will ensure we get there.

The Head of Music will build on our momentum and help shape the future of our rapidly growing music business, driving a unified strategy for our B2B, artist-focused, and creator/consumer offerings. They will oversee music product, licensing, marketing, and partnerships. They will also work hand-in-hand with our GTM and FDE teams on the sale and implementation of our music tools. In addition, they will represent ElevenLabs at industry and tech events globally. This is a singular role for an exceptional individual with deep experience, ties, and respect across the music industry.

Requirements

  • Can craft and execute a cohesive strategy across B2B, artist, and consumer music tools, including product, licensing, marketing, partnerships, and sales. Should personally spike in at least one of these disciplines.

  • Proven track record of driving the development of music technology, including excellent product sense.

  • Deep knowledge of licensing across the recorded music and publishing industries.

  • Experience with marketing music technology products.

  • Leadership and management experience.

  • Comfort with public speaking.

Location

This role is remote and can be executed globally, but San Francisco, New York, and London are preferred.

We are an equal opportunity employer and do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability or other legally protected statuses.

description:

Du willst Marketing nicht nur in der Vorlesung hören, sondern wirklich machen?
Du hast Lust, in Zahlen einzutauchen, kreativ zu werden und im Team Kampagnen aufzubauen, die vor allem unsere DACH-Crowd aktivieren? Dann passt du ziemlich gut zu uns.
Bei Invesdor, Europas führender Impact-Investmentplattform, verbinden wir Rendite mit Wirkung. Über unsere Plattform investieren Menschen in Unternehmen, die die Welt ein Stück besser machen wollen – von erneuerbaren Energien bis hin zu MedTech und EdTech.


Deine Aufgaben

Als Werkstudent:in im Marketing bist du mittendrin statt nur dabei. Du arbeitest an Kampagnen, die unsere Projekte sichtbar machen, stärkst unsere Marke im DACH-Raum und begeisterst unsere Crowd mit passendem Content. Von Anfang an bekommst du eigene, klar umrissene Aufgabenbereiche und übernimmst nach und nach kleine Projekte selbst – natürlich mit Rückhalt durch das Team.

Deine Aufgaben: von Zahlen bis DACH-Activation
Deine Rolle ist bewusst breit angelegt. Je nach Projekt unterstützt du unser Marketingteam zum Beispiel bei:
Content & Creation

  • Erstellung von Grafiken und Visuals in Canva für Social Media, Newsletter und Online-Kampagnen
  • Unterstützung bei Google Ads und Social-Media-Anzeigen (z. B. Textentwürfe, Bildformate, Vorbereitung von A/B-Tests)
  • Mitarbeit bei der Pflege unserer Kanäle wie LinkedIn oder Instagram – mit besonderem Fokus auf unsere DACH-Zielgruppen
  • Unterstützung bei der Erstellung von Landingpages, Blogbeiträgen oder E-Mail-Kampagnen zur Aktivierung unserer Crowd
DACH-Crowd & Partner-Aktivierung
  • Mitarbeit bei der Entwicklung und Umsetzung von Maßnahmen zur Aktivierung unserer DACH-Crowd (z. B. Kampagnen, Newsletter-Specials, Community-Formate)
  • Recherche, Ansprache und Betreuung potenzieller Affiliate- und Kooperationspartner (z. B. Plattformen, Blogs, Communities)
  • Unterstützung bei gemeinsamen Marketingaktionen mit Partnern (z. B. Co-Branded Content, Social-Media-Kooperationen, Webinare)
Zahlen & Analyse
  • Unterstützung beim KPI-Tracking und bei einfachen Reportings (z. B. Kampagnen-Performance, Klickzahlen, Conversion Rates)
  • Auswertung von Maßnahmen und Ableitung erster Empfehlungen: Was lief gut, was können wir verbessern?
  • Unterstützung beim Monitoring unserer Marketing-Aktivitäten in der DACH-Region
Eigene Projekte
  • Übernahme eines eigenen kleinen Projekts, z. B. die Betreuung eines Social-Media-Formats, eines Newsletters oder einer Affiliate-Aktion
  • Verantwortung für Planung, Umsetzung und ein einfaches Reporting – mit Feedback und Sparring aus dem Team
Strategie & Ideen
  • Mitarbeit bei der Entwicklung kreativer Ideen, wie wir unsere internationale – insbesondere DACH – Crowd noch besser aktivieren können
  • Teilnahme an Brainstormings zu neuen Formaten, Kampagnen oder Storytelling-Ansätzen
  • Schnittstelle zu anderen Teams in Finnland, Deutschland und den Niederlanden, um Inhalte und Projekte abzustimmen
Keine Sorge: Du musst nicht alles schon perfekt können. Wichtig ist, dass du neugierig bist, Lust hast, dich reinzufuchsen und Schritt für Schritt mehr Verantwortung zu übernehmen.


Das bieten wir Dir

  • Du bekommst eine feste Ansprechperson im Marketing, die dich beim Onboarding und in deinen Projekten begleitet.
  • Regelmäßige kurze Feedback-Gespräche helfen dir, dich fachlich und persönlich weiterzuentwickeln.
  • Wenn du möchtest, kannst du auch in andere Bereiche reinschnuppern (z. B. Produkt, Sales oder Investor Relations), um das große Ganze besser zu verstehen.
  • Einblicke in wirklich breites Marketing – von Performance & KPIs bis hin zu kreativen Konzepten
  • Arbeiten in einem internationalen Umfeld mit Kolleg:innen aus verschiedenen Ländern
  • Ein motiviertes Team mit flachen Hierarchien und viel Raum für deine eigenen Ideen
  • Ein Arbeitsplatz zentral am Ku’damm in Berlin plus die Möglichkeit zum Homeoffice
  • Klare Wochenstunden, die zu deinem Studium passen (z. B. ca. 15–20 Stunden pro Woche, in den Semesterferien gern auch mehr)
  • Flexibilität in Prüfungsphasen: In Klausurenzeiten kannst du deine Stunden in Absprache mit uns anpassen.
  • Eine offene, lockere Arbeitsatmosphäre – wir duzen uns alle und Entscheidungswege sind wirklich kurz.

Lust bekommen?
Dann schick uns deine Unterlagen (kurzes Anschreiben, Lebenslauf, relevante Zeugnisse und deinen frühestmöglichen Starttermin) an: ----- du möchtest, kannst du auch direkt ein oder zwei Arbeitsproben mitschicken, zum Beispiel:
 
  • Grafiken aus Canva
  • Social-Media-Posts
  • ein Uni-Projekt (z. B. Kampagnenkonzept oder Analyse)

Über Aampere

Werde Teil von Aampere, einem Seed-Stage VC-backed Startup, das den europäischen Markt für gebrauchte E-Autos neu definiert. Wir ermöglichen EV-Besitzern einen Verkauf innerhalb von 48 Stunden und geben Händlern in ganz Europa Zugang zu neuen Kundengruppen. Der Markt ist fragmentiert, undurchsichtig und schwer vertrauenswürdig. Wir bauen die Infrastruktur, die das löst, damit mehr E-Autos ein zweites Leben bekommen und der Umstieg auf Elektro wirklich Fahrt aufnimmt.

Und es funktioniert: Jahr für Jahr vervierfachen wir unseren Umsatz und halten bereits über 1% der Wiederverkäufe von E-Autos an Endkunden in Deutschland. Unser Team kommt aus der deutschen Startup-Szene und der Automobilwelt, mit Erfahrung bei Autarc, Limehome, Cardino, Wemolo, Alasco, Porsche, Mercedes und KPMG.

Ein Logenplatz dafür, wie ein Startup gebaut und geführt wird. Du bist die rechte Hand unseres Chief of Staff, Benni, der Mitarbeiter Nummer eins bei einem YC-backed Startup war und vor Aampere bei mehreren Top-Tier-VC-Startups gearbeitet hat. Du sitzt dort, wo das Unternehmen gesteuert wird, arbeitest über alle Funktionen hinweg und übernimmst echte Verantwortung ab der ersten Woche. Wenn du lernen willst, wie man ein Startup von innen betreibt, von People über GTM und Finance bis Ops, gibt es kaum bessere Plätze.


Deine Mission

Bau die Organisation mit uns, nicht für uns. Wir verantworten die People-Funktion und skalieren gerade unseren Headcount stark, während wir die Strukturen bauen, die die nächste Welle an Hires trägt. Du sitzt mitten in diesem Aufbau und ownst echte Teile davon, statt sie von der Seite zu beobachten.
Sitz dort, wo gesteuert wird. Die Chief-of-Staff-Rolle lebt zwischen den OKRs der Gründer und den Ownern, die sie liefern, und fordert und befähigt beide Seiten. Du bist in diesen Runden dabei, siehst, wie Prioritäten gesetzt und auf die Probe gestellt werden, und bildest dir dein eigenes Urteil darüber, was das Geschäft wirklich bewegt.
Übernimm die Sonderprojekte end to end. Ein großer Teil der Arbeit ist Zero to One und passt noch in keine saubere Stellenbeschreibung, vom Aufbau des B2B-Angebots bis zu unseren PR- und Comms-Strukturen. Die Liste ändert sich ständig, und du bringst Themen von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung.
Arbeite im Startup-Tempo. Vieles passiert ad hoc, Entscheidungen fallen schnell, und wir erwarten eine Get-things-done-Mentalität. Du bringst Struktur rein, schließt die Lücken und wartest nicht, bis man dir sagt, was zu tun ist.


Das bringst du mit

Du bist Generalist und denkst in Ownership. Du siehst die Lücke und schließt sie. Du bringst Ordnung in unübersichtliche Probleme, ohne dass man dich darum bittet, und bist am stärksten, wenn der Weg noch nicht vorgezeichnet ist.
Du hast schon auf Top-Niveau geliefert. Frisch von einer Top-Universität, mit einem Track Record bei einer führenden Beratung oder einem Top-Tier-Startup. Du arbeitest über deinem Level, und das kannst du belegen.
Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch. Du wechselst mühelos zwischen deutschsprachiger Partner- und Kandidatenkommunikation und einem englischsprachigen Team.
Du willst eine Karriere, keinen Sommerjob. Das ist ein sechsmonatiges Vollzeit-Praktikum, und wenn du herausragend bist, wollen wir dich halten. Komm mit dem Gedanken rein, wohin das führt, nicht wo es endet.


Aampere ist nichts für dich wenn...

...du überwiegend remote arbeiten willst. Wir glauben, dass die besten Ideen entstehen, wenn Menschen im selben Raum sind. Deshalb bist du mindestens vier Tage pro Woche bei uns im Office.
...du fertige Prozesse und Strukturen vorfinden willst. Bei uns gibt es vieles davon noch nicht. Wir suchen Leute, die Strukturen und Prozesse selbst bauen, statt sie zu verwalten.
...du einen fertigen Plan brauchst, bevor du loslegst. Seed Stage heißt: vieles ist unklar und ändert sich wöchentlich. Du musst dich wohl damit fühlen, im Ungewissen zu entscheiden und unterwegs zu korrigieren.
...du in deiner Lane bleiben willst. "Das ist nicht mein Job" kennen wir nicht. Du packst da an, wo es brennt, auch wenn es außerhalb deiner Rollenbeschreibung liegt.
...du einen klassischen 9-to-5-Job willst. Wir bauen etwas Großes und das geht nicht nebenbei. Wer hier ist, will Vollgas geben, statt nur die Zeit abzusitzen.


Why Aampere?

Startup Umfeld: Jeden Tag etwas bewirken und gemeinsam mit uns die Welt elektrisieren.
Persönliches Wachstum: Im schnelllebigen Umfeld kannst du schnell aufsteigen und Verantwortung übernehmen.
Urban Sports Club oder Job Ticket: healthy team, happy team.
Late Dinner im Office: Wenn es abends länger wird, übernehmen wir dein Dinner (Uber Eats).
Offsite: bis jetzt waren wir am Lago Maggiore, in den Alpen und am Tegernsee, what's next?
EV fahren: Bald kannst du unseren Aampere-gebrandeten VW ID.Buzz fahren.
Wohnen im Werksviertel: Im angrenzenden Co-Living Space gibt es die Möglichkeit, eigenständig ein Zimmer zu mieten, direkt neben dem Aampere-Büro und mit Blick auf das Riesenrad.
Perspektive: Stellst du dich als Hell Yes heraus, ist eine Übernahme in eine Festanstellung nach dem Praktikum möglich.

Das Praktikum ist ab sofort für 6 Monate zu besetzen. Wenn du etwas bewegen möchtest, dann werde Teil unseres Teams.


Noch ein paar Worte zum Abschluss

Bewirb dich jetzt! Wir freuen uns über Deine formlose Bewerbung, alles weitere besprechen wir gemeinsam.
Egal, welchen Hintergrund, welche Herkunft oder welche Geschlechtsidentität du mitbringst – bei uns zählt, wer du als Person bist. Wir fördern eine Kultur des Respekts und Miteinanders, in der jede Stimme gehört wird, persönliche Weiterentwicklung möglich ist und Wertschätzung an erster Stelle steht.

description:
About The Role

Vivid Money is redefining how modern corporates, holding structures, and financial institutions manage and optimize their capital. From institutional-grade Treasury products (high-yield Interest Accounts, Money Market Funds, and ETFs) to multi-currency infrastructure and FX solutions, we provide the financial architecture that traditional banks make too slow and expensive.
We are expanding our institutional footprint in Germany.
We aren’t looking for a standard software sales rep; we are looking for a New Business Account Executive who understands the fabric of the German financial ecosystem. You will be employee number one on the ground, tasked with unlocking high-value segments: PE/VC funds, holding companies (Soparfis), family offices, and corporate service providers.
If you have the network to navigate corporate Germany, understand structured finance/treasury needs, and want the autonomy to build a market from scratch, this role is for you.


Your Mission

  • Originate Institutional Pipeline: Identify and engage decision-makers across Germanys unique B2B landscape, focusing on PE/VC funds, corporate holding structures, asset managers, and corporates.
  • Leverage Channel Partnerships: Build strategic relationships with local multipliers—accountants, tax advisors, law firms—who manage hundreds of entities requiring modern treasury setups.
  • Navigate Complex Sales Cycles: Run the end-to-end commercial cycle for high-value accounts, from sophisticated discovery and structured treasury pitches to compliance onboarding and closing.
  • Position Vivid as a Yield Partner: Educate fund managers and corporate treasurers on how to leverage Vivid’s Treasury and MMF solutions to optimize returns on their cash reserves and dry powder.
  • Shape the German Playbook: Partner directly with the Sales Leadership team to refine our Ideal Customer Profile (ICP), localized messaging, and regulatory positioning for the German market.
  • Represent the Brand: Act as the face of Vivid Money GmbH at major financial services, fund industry, and fintech events in Germany.


Your Profile

  • 5+ years of B2B/Institutional sales experience within the German financial ecosystem (e.g., Private Banking, Corporate Banking, Fund Services, FinTech, or Treasury/Asset Management).
  • Deep local knowledge: You thoroughly understand Germanys financial structures (Soparfis, RAIFs, SICAVs) and know how these entities manage liquidity and banking relationships.
  • An established network: You have an existing book of contacts or a proven ability to network into CFOs, Fund Operations leads, Managing Directors, and Domiciliation Agents.
  • Technical fluency: You can speak confidently about FX, money market funds, yield generation, and compliance/KYB processes for complex corporate structures.
  • Entrepreneurial mindset: You thrive in an "AI-first," high-autonomy environment where the playbook is yours to write.
  • Languages: Full professional fluency in English and German is required. 


Why Join Vivid?

  • Hybrid or remote way of work. You can work from our Berlin office or fully remote from other locations. 
  • Direct influence on go-to-market strategy and revenue growth. 
  • Significant ownership from day one and strong growth opportunities. 
  • AI-first culture – we use it every day, not just talk about it.
  • Learning & development budget to support your professional growth. 
  • Fully paid vacation and sick leave. 
  • Sports compensation. 
  • Real growth prospects, significant responsibility, and the ability to make an immediate impact from day one.


Compensation range

Total target compensation: €110,000–€120,000 gross annually (base salary + performance-related bonus). Final compensation is determined individually, based on your experience, skills, and the scope of the role, assessed against objective, gender-neutral criteria.


About Vivid

At Vivid, we're on a mission to change how businesses and individuals manage their money across Europe. For businesses, we build tools that actually make a difference: multi-IBAN accounts, high-yield savings, business cashback, team cards, and accounting integrations that save real time — all in one place. And for individuals, we offer a simple way to manage and grow your wealth: access to global stocks, ETFs and 150+ cryptocurrencies, cashback, and personalised financial insights.

Our mission? Your success. Everyone deserves the chance to see their finances flourish, and we're dedicated to empowering our customers to make this a reality.

Founded in 2019 in Berlin by Alexander Emeshev and Artem Iamanov, Vivid has quickly grown into one of Germany's top financial platforms for SMEs and private accounts. Since then, we've expanded rapidly across Europe, earning the trust of over 500,000 customers — and with over €200 million raised and a valuation of €775 million, we're just getting started.

We're building Vivid as an AI-native organization — across every function, from product to compliance to operations. Automation handles a growing share of day-to-day execution. For us, this means our teams can focus on architecture, strategy, and high-impact decision-making. This changes how we work: less manual execution, more ownership in building systems that scale. We want to help define what AI-native looks like in a regulated financial environment — and we're looking for people who want to build that future with us.

Process

Was fehlt, ist ein integriertes System, das diesen Wandel wirtschaftlich und operativ beherrschbar macht.

VREY kombiniert zertifizierten Messstellenbetrieb mit eigener Software und ermöglicht Eigentümern erstmals, ihren selbst erzeugten Solarstrom direkt an ihre Mieter zu verkaufen – einfach und ohne selbst zum Energieversorger zu werden (§42b EnWG).

Damit wird regulatorischer Zwang zu einer profitablen und planbaren Chance:

  • Zweistellige Renditen und Wertsteigerung für Eigentümer,

  • ~20 % Stromkostenersparnis für Mieter, und

  • digitale Infrastruktur für Speicher, Wärmepumpen und Flexibilität.

Bereits heute betreuen wir eine dreistellige Anzahl an Projekten - darunter die größten Bestandshalter und Wohnungsbaugenossenschaften - in allen 16 Bundesländern. Damit gehören wir nach kürzester Zeit zu den führenden Anbietern im Markt.

Im Zuge unserer Seed-Finanzierung haben wir 3,3 Mio. € von führenden Impact- und Energy-VCs (u. a. Rubio Impact Ventures, HTGF, Kopa Ventures) eingesammelt. Mit dem frischen Kapital gehen wir in die nächste Wachstumsphase und bauen unser Team gezielt aus.

Wir stehen am Anfang eines strukturellen Marktumbruchs. Wer heute die Energieinfrastruktur im Mehrfamilienhaus definiert, prägt sie für Jahrzehnte. Werde Teil von VREY und baue mit uns das führende EnergyOS.

  • Erfahrung oder starkes Interesse an Datenanalyse, Automatisierung und KI/LLM-Agents (z. B. Python, APIs, Umgang mit größeren Datenmengen)

  • Du suchst bewusst keinen 9-to-5-Job, sondern willst in einem schnelllebigen, gründer-nahen Umfeld Verantwortung übernehmen, Strukturen aufbauen und das Wachstum aktiv mitgestalten

Deine Aufgaben

Mission der Rolle

Du sitzt an einer unternehmenskritischen Schnittstelle: tief drin im operativen Energiedaten-Geschäft und mit dem Mandat, dieses Geschäft durch eigene Datenanalysen, Tools und KI-Agenten grundlegend zu automatisieren. Du siehst den unmittelbaren Effekt deiner Arbeit - jedes gelöste Ticket bringt ein Projekt näher an die Abrechnung, jeder gebaute Agent spart dem ganzen Team Zeit.

1. Datenanalyse & Automatisierung durch eigene KI-Agents

  • Du analysierst Messwerte, Zählerstände und Versandjobs auf Muster, Ausreißer und wiederkehrende Fehlerursachen

  • Du übersetzt dieses Wissen in KI-Agenten, die Fehler eigenständig diagnostizieren und Lösungswege vorschlagen oder umsetzen

  • Du bist der fachliche Motor der Messstellenbetrieb (MSB) App: du erkennst aus dem Tagesgeschäft, welche Features fehlen, spezifizierst sie und bringst sie mittels eigener Entwicklung ins Produkt

2. Operative Energiedaten-Verantwortung bis zur Abrechnungsreife

  • Du bringst Projekte Monat für Monat zur Abrechnungsreife: fehlende oder unplausible Messwerte korrigieren, Ersatzwerte über Referenzprofile bilden, Werte maskieren und neu berechnen lassen

  • Du legst Versandjobs an, überwachst deren Status und plausibilisierst die Daten nach jedem Fix

  • Du arbeitest dabei täglich in der App unserer Partner und unserer internen MSB App entlang der marktüblichen MSB-Prozesse

  • Du verantwortest alle Energiedaten-Tickets intern (Projekt- und Abrechnungsteams) wie extern (VNB, Lieferanten, ÜNB) - von Annahme über Priorisierung bis Lösung - und bist Eskalationsinstanz bei komplexen Fällen

Weitere Vorteile: Tägliche Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern, Getränke & Snacks, Personalverantwortung und die Möglichkeit, das Unternehmen von Grund auf mitzugestalten

Das Wichtigste: Du brennst für Unternehmertum und Start-ups. Noch ein paar Worte zum Schluss

Bei VREY sind wir davon überzeugt, dass Vielfalt uns als Unternehmen und Gesellschaft stärkt. Weder bei der Einstellung noch während des Beschäftigungsverhältnisses werden Entscheidungen auf Basis von Hautfarbe, Religion oder religiösen Glaubens, ethnischer oder nationaler Herkunft, Behinderung oder Alter getroffen.

Auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen erfüllst, zögere nicht, dich trotzdem zu bewerben. Wenn du von unserer Mission begeistert bist und glaubst, einen Beitrag leisten zu können, möchten wir von dir hören!

Der beste Weg ist eine warme Intro: Kennst du jemand, der auf diese Rolle passt? Empfiehl die Person und erhalte 3.000€ bei erfolgreicher Einstellung.

  • Landingpages und Funnels bauen wir mit. Ein Creative verkauft nur so gut wie die Seite dahinter.

  • Creative Strategist, Copywriter, Grafiker und Videografen im eigenen Haus. Kein Warten auf externe Zulieferer, dazu ein AI-Stack für mehr Output.

Genau dafür suchen wir jemanden.

Was dich hier erwartet

Du übernimmst nicht ein paar Werbekonten. Du übernimmst Verantwortung für das Wachstum deiner Kunden über Social Ads und entwickelst eigenständig die richtige Strategie.

Denn wir arbeiten nicht mit Kunden zusammen, um Kampagnen zu verwalten. Wir arbeiten mit ihnen, um sie zum Wachsen zu bringen.

Was das im Alltag heißt:

  • Du planst und steuerst die Paid-Social-Kampagnen auf Meta und TikTok, von der Strategie bis zur täglichen Optimierung

  • Du skalierst Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets. Die Zielmetrik ist Profitabilität, nicht Ad Spend.

  • Du entwickelst die Creative-Konzepte mit Anna und dem Creative Team. UGC, Founder Ads und Statics entstehen aus Testdaten, nicht aus Bauchgefühl.

  • Du lieferst die Ideen für Ads und Funnels nach Direct-Response-Prinzipien. Unser Team setzt sie um und arbeitet sie im Detail aus.

  • Du sorgst dafür, dass Hooks, Formate und Narrative laufend getestet werden. Ein Gewinner-Creative hält auf hohen Ad-Spend-Leveln nicht lange.

  • Du führst die wöchentlichen Kundenreportings und berätst auf Entscheiderebene, nicht nur zum Kanal

  • Du baust den Social Ads Bereich weiter aus, über SOPs, Qualitätsmanagement und die fachliche Führung neuer Teammitglieder

Der letzte Punkt ist uns wichtig. Diese Rolle gibt es bei EVOLVE einmal. Deshalb suchen wir jemanden, der die Verantwortung für das gesamte Paid Social Team übernehmen will und sich perspektivisch als Paid Social Lead entwickelt.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Mindestens drei Jahre Erfahrung im Performance Marketing mit Schwerpunkt Paid Social, als Hauptkanal und nicht nebenbei

  • Nachweisbare Skalierung von E-Commerce-Accounts auf hohe fünf- bis sechsstellige Monatsbudgets

  • Tiefes Wissen im Meta Business Manager, idealerweise auch im TikTok Ads Manager. Dazu Routine mit Tracking-Tools wie Triple Whale, Admetrics oder Tracify

  • Sicherer Umgang mit Margen, Deckungsbeiträgen, CAC und POAS. Ohne diese Zahlen lässt sich profitabel nicht skalieren

  • Strategisches Verständnis für E-Commerce. Du denkst über den Werbekanal hinaus und steuerst Projekte entlang des gesamten Kundengeschäfts

  • Verständnis für Direct-Response-Mechanismen, UGC-Formate und Founder Ads. Du erkennst, warum ein Creative verkauft, und nicht nur, dass es verkauft

  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachniveau für Kundenkommunikation und Copy-Bewertung. Englisch fließend für die Arbeit in den Ad-Managern

  • Sehr gute Selbstorganisation, auch weil wir 100 % remote arbeiten

  • Idealerweise erste Erfahrung in fachlicher Führung oder im Mentoring von Junioren

Direkt gesagt: Dieser Job passt nicht zu jedem

Du solltest dich nicht bewerben, wenn du keine E-Commerce-Erfahrung mitbringst. Wir suchen jemanden, der Accounts auf exzellentem Niveau steuert. Fachlich challengen wir dich gern. Das E-Commerce-Know-how solltest du jedoch schon mitbringen.

Der Rahmen

  • 100 % Remote seit Tag 1, kein Hybrid-Kompromiss

  • 30 Tage Urlaub

  • Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung

  • Weiterbildungsbudget sowie Unterstützung durch interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite

  • Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack

  • Zweimal jährlich Teamevents und Workations

So läuft der Prozess

Deine Bewerbung. Dein Lebenslauf reicht. Wenn wir Rückfragen haben, schicken wir dir einen kurzen Fragebogen.

Erstgespräch. Ein kurzes Video-Gespräch mit Vanessa aus unserem HR: gegenseitiges Kennenlernen, Rahmen und Erwartungen.

Fachgespräch. Hier geht es in die Tiefe, mit der Geschäftsführung oder dem Lead deines Fachbereichs.

Finales Kennenlernen. Mit der Geschäftsführung und deinem zukünftigen Ansprechpartner, persönlich und fachlich. Hier definieren wir deine Stelle noch einmal genau auf Basis deiner Stärken und Interessen.

Entscheidung und Start. Wir entscheiden schnell und planen dein Onboarding gemeinsam.

Deine Entwicklung bei uns

Kurzfristig, die ersten zwei Monate. Einarbeitung in die EVOLVE-Methodik und unsere Prozesse. Du übernimmst erste Accounts gemeinsam mit dem Team.

Mittelfristig. Volle Verantwortung für mehrere High-Budget-Accounts. Du steuerst das Paid-Social-Team fachlich und onboardest ein weiteres Teammitglied.

Langfristig. Du führst als Paid Social Lead den gesamten Social Ads Bereich, fachlich und disziplinarisch, bis zu zehn Personen.

Lead the growth of an established business with significant market potential.

Represent an established portfolio of high-quality infrastructure solutions with strong references across Europe.

Spire Global is a leading provider of space-based data, analytics, and services, helping organizations make better decisions with insights from our constellation of satellites. We are committed to operational excellence, compliance, and maintaining the highest standards of internal control.

As a Senior Systems Engineer, you will be responsible for the technical outcome of complex space missions. During mission contracting and requirements development, you may work with the sales engineering org to ensure mission requirements are valid and mission scope is adequately defined. Systems Engineers translate higher level requirements down to lower-level requirements, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary.  

You will be the overall technical lead responsible for "building the right thing" and "building it right". This will include the management of system requirements, technical budgets, and sub-system interfaces.  Your responsibility extends to ensuring there is sufficient verification and testing of the system, and you will take ownership of the technical performance outcomes for the mission. You will also act as the technical point of contact for Spire's global customers during mission development phases and through on-orbit validation of the space systems, working with Spire project and program managers to provide effective communication where required. 

Your knowledge and experience working across multiple technical disciplines will help you coordinate Spire's technical efforts to ensure ultimate mission success. 

Role Responsibilities:

  • Take overall technical ownership of Spire Space and/or Ground Systems from technical development through on-orbit verification; ensure that we are "building the right thing" and "building it right".
  • Lead requirements management for a given mission or program - including development, validation, verification, and change management.
  • Lead technical risk management for a given mission or program - including identification, qualification, mitigation, and resolution.
  • Develop top-level requirements and then flow-down to lower-levels, consulting and collaborating with discipline team-leads and subject matter experts where necessary.
  • Serve as the primary Spire technical POC to customers and contractors - communicating and advocating on behalf of internal technical teams where necessary.

  • Proactively communicate to program/project managers where changes in scope, requirements, expected system performance, or development outcomes impact the mission.
  • Develop, deliver, and maintain mission documentation required to support programs or missions, including both internal and external (customer- or contractor-facing) documentation.
  • Support the sales engineering team in the development of technical concepts and budgets, feasibility assessments, requirements, scope, and documentation needed during the sales cycle.

  • BSc in Engineering, Computer Science, equivalent STEM-related subject, or equivalent work experience.
  • 5+ years of experience working in a technical engineering discipline (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, RF Communications, etc) or as a systems engineer for complex integrated systems.
  • Comprehensive understanding of space systems, concepts of operations, and remote systems operation.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience as a space systems engineer working across engineering disciplines (Mechanical, Electrical, Software, Controls, Radio/Comms, etc)
  • Experience developing or integrating RF and optical payloads.
  • Experience participating in architecture and design of digital systems including ground station networks, data distribution and data processing systems, and spacecraft data handling systems
  • Experience coordinating or leading diverse technical teams spanning multiple engineering disciplines and time zones
  • Strong interpersonal skills for building relationships with clients and effectively communicating with other members of cross-functional teams

  • Experience in satellite mission design, development, and testing with a clear understanding of major mission design trades and scope drivers (power / payload duty cycle, communications systems / data budgets, ground stations, launch and environmental loads, EMI/EMC, thermal management, etc.)

title: Growth Specialist
description:
Got Drive? Join AnyVan as we make moving anything, anywhere miles better and build a career that moves just as fast.


Back in 2009, our CEO Angus saw half-empty vans everywhere and knew there had to be a better way! That's how AnyVan began. He set out to create the world's most efficient logistics technology and help halve the number of wasted miles by filling those empty vans.


Since then we've become the nation's favourite way to move, with over 150k five-star reviews and 5 million customers in the UK and Europe. Our team of 400 AnyVanners across London, Cape Town and Bogota is proving that moving doesn't have to cost the earth by helping save 8,520 tonnes of Carbon each year.

We are looking for a Growth Specialist to execute alongside our senior leaders and run the projects that matter most to our global expansion. You won’t be boxed into a specific geography, a single channel, or a swim lane. Instead, you operate as an execution fixer: you will deploy wherever the highest-leverage growth opportunities are, working in tandem with marketing, product, sales, and operations to turn hypotheses into real, commercial results.

Working closely with our Growth Lead, you will be a vital driver behind our most critical initiatives. We aren't looking for coordinators to manage agency timelines, format status decks, or update ticket backlogs. We need a commercial operator who brings analytical agility, a fierce bias for action, and zero fear of moving fast in the gray area. This is the ultimate blend of sharp execution and directly driving the plot forward early in your career.

The core of the role:

  • Own the Outcome: You are responsible for hitting the targets inside your current project. If a blocker pops up, you don't wait for permission or an instruction manual, you collaborate across teams, find a workaround, and keep moving.

  • Seek the Paths that Scale: We focus on the chunky things that have a material impact. You’ll help ship experiments fast, read the immediate feedback loops, and help build the foundations for repeatable growth playbooks.

  • Commercial Focus: We don't live in a world of vanity metrics. Your success will be measured on hard outcomes: volume of users acquired, conversion rates, CAC efficiency, and revenue generated.

  • Using AI vs talking about it: We are an AI-native team. You won't be using it just to tidy up copy or format slides; you will use AI tools creatively from day one to execute execution tasks in minutes that take traditional teams days, maximizing your velocity.

What you'll be doing:

  • Executing critical campaigns: Take ownership of driving specific, high-priority customer segments. Examples could be launching a localized acquisition campaign, building the machine to acquire SMEs, or owning the playbook to rapidly scale student acquisition.

  • Creating leverage across teams: You won't be siloed in marketing. You’ll work alongside product, sales, and operations to ship experiments, gather feedback, and ensure your growth sprints are delivered smoothly.

  • Interrogating the data: You will live in the numbers. While we have data experts, you need to be comfortable pulling and manipulating raw performance data yourself to find out why a campaign is or isn't converting.

  • Moving at pace and taking intelligent risks: You'll build and ship a scrappy V1 of an idea today, look at the data tomorrow, and iterate. You don't stall out waiting for perfect information, you learn by doing it for real.

  • Please note we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role at this time.

Skills and experience you'll need:

  • A startup mindset: 3+ years of experience in growth, performance marketing, BizOps, or consulting. Side hustles or personal building projects are a massive plus.

  • Commercial fluency: You understand the connection between execution and the bottom line. You are highly analytical and comfortable diving deep into a spreadsheet to track campaign economics.

  • Broad curiosity: You don't want to be pigeonholed as just a copywriter or just a paid social manager. You want exposure across the full stack of growth and commercial levers.

  • Obsession with speed: You love seeing your work go live immediately. You get genuinely frustrated by slow corporate approval chains and unnecessary red tape.

  • Act like a founder: Self-motivated, comfortable with pressure, and ready to roll up your sleeves to get things done, vs a ‘but that’s not my job’ vibe.

We don’t chase hype cycles. We innovate, build and deploy responsible AI which moves the needle - and we know a thing or two about doing it well. We bring an unparalleled depth of technical, product and delivery expertise to our clients who span government, finance, retail, energy, life sciences and defence.

Our business, and reputation, is growing fast and we’re always on the lookout for individuals who share our intellectual curiosity and desire to build a positive legacy through technology.

AI is an epoch-defining technology, join a company where you’ll be empowered to envision its most powerful applications, and to make them happen.

About the role

As a Research Scientist at Faculty, you will conduct original technical research in AI safety to build the foundation for safe, trustworthy AI deployment. Operating at the forefront of AI, you will design and execute impactful experiments, study model behavior, and develop robust, reproducible tooling. Working alongside Senior and Lead Research Scientists, you will bridge scientific discovery with practical application, helping translate complex technical insights for external partners, frontier labs, and national security institutes. This is an incredible opportunity to hone your expertise, shape emerging safety standards, and solve some of the most critical challenges in modern AI.

What you'll be doing:

  • Executing technical research in AI safety by designing and running experiments to study and steer model behavior.

  • Applying white-box and black-box methodologies, focusing on interpretability, steering, and behavioral studies of transformer-based LLMs.

  • Developing high-quality, modular, and reproducible research code in Python using deep learning frameworks like PyTorch.

  • Building and maintaining research infrastructure and technical tooling to accelerate scientific discovery.

  • Documenting and communicating experimental findings through high-quality academic papers, technical reports, and presentations.

  • Collaborating with senior scientists to identify literature gaps, refine hypotheses, and identify research scope.

  • Translating complex technical insights for diverse audiences, including external frontier labs, government bodies, and safety institutes.

Who we're looking for:

  • Solid background in machine learning fundamentals and transformer architectures (specifically LLMs).

  • A practical understanding of white-box and black-box interpretability techniques, such as steering vectors or mechanistic interpretability.

  • Demonstrated capability to take structured technical problems and formulate hypotheses

  • Strong programming skills in Python and deep learning frameworks like PyTorch, with a track record of writing clean, modular research code, using Git for version control.

  • Excellent communication, enabling you to translate complex technical concepts and experimental results into clear reports and presentations.

  • Curiosity and analytical rigour, combined with exposure to core AI safety areas such as robustness, evaluations, or uncertainty calibration.

Our Recruitment Ethos

We aim to grow the best team - not the most similar one. We know that diversity of individuals fosters diversity of thought, and that strengthens our principle of seeking truth. And we know from experience that diverse teams deliver better work, relevant to the world in which we live. We’re united by a deep intellectual curiosity and desire to use our abilities for measurable positive impact. We strongly encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, religions and sexual orientations.

Some of our standout benefits:

  • Private healthcare and dental

  • Enhanced parental leave

  • Family-Friendly Flexibility & Flexible working

  • Hybrid Working

If you don’t feel you meet all the requirements, but are excited by the role and know you bring some key strengths, please don't hesitate in applying as you might be right for this role, or other roles. We are open to conversations about part-time hours.
